olivia: Quick follow-up to the stream-retry RFC — I sketched a small proposal for how the edge should treat trailers and where retry/resume responsibility lives. TL;DR: edge should treat trailers as authoritative final status and only attempt retries/resumes when the upstream advertises explicit resume semantics.
raj: +1 to making trailers authoritative. A few concrete rules we should consider:
- If the connection terminates before any trailer -> network error -> safe for edge to retry (subject to idempotency)
- If trailer present with explicit final-status header -> act on that (no retry)
- If trailer contains resume-token -> allow resume from token (no full replay)
marco: Quick concern: how do we avoid double-executing side effects? We need a clear idempotency boundary. Proposal: require an Idempotency-Key for any request the edge is allowed to replay end-to-end. For streaming writes/side-effect ops, only allow resume semantics (resume-token) — full replay only if Idempotency-Key present.
zhen: +1. Also: define header names and short semantics so SDKs can rely on them. I'm thinking:
```
Idempotency-Key: <uuid>
X-Redwood-Resume-Token: <opaque>
X-Redwood-Final-Status: ok|retryable_error|nonretryable_error|partial
```
Edge behaviour:
- If X-Redwood-Final-Status is nonretryable_error -> surface to client, no retry
- If retryable_error or connection reset before trailer -> attempt retry if Idempotency-Key present, else fail
- If X-Redwood-Resume-Token present -> attempt resume from token (no replay)
olivia: I like that. Two subtle things: 1) clients may disconnect and reconnect mid-stream — we must decide if edge buffers anything to allow quick resume versus always asking upstream for resume-token. 2) billing semantics: partial responses + retries need deterministic token accounting.
raj: For disconnects: prefer stateless resume when possible. Upstream should issue a resume-token periodically (eg every N tokens or on chunk boundaries). Edge will surface the latest resume-token to the client in a trailer or via a checkpoint websocket event. That avoids edge having to buffer large payloads.
For billing: edge should record consumed tokens per request idempotency key and mark them as billed once upstream commits final-status ok. Retries using the same Idempotency-Key should reference the same billing record (no double-bill). If resume-token used, bill only for delta tokens returned to client.
marco: One more: what about interactions with partial caching? If upstream can serve partial cached prefixes and then fast-resume the rest, we should standardize a trailer flag `x-rw-cacheable-prefix: yes|no` so edge can populate cache for prefixes safely.
zhen: Good call. Add to header list:
```
X-Redwood-Cacheable-Prefix: yes|no
```
Edge only writes prefix to cache if final-status is ok or if cacheable-prefix=yes AND resume-token present.
deploy-bot: deploy-checklist: updated config flags: ``edge.resume.enabled``, ``edge.idempotency.strict``; migration plan: rollout to canary 25% then 100% if metrics stable. :robot_face:
olivia: Decision draft for RFC update (for visibility):
1) Trailers are authoritative for final status. Edge must not retry after a trailer unless trailer explicitly indicates retryable_error and upstream says it can accept replay (Idempotency-Key) or has provided resume-token.
2) Resume-token is the only mechanism to do partial resume without full replay. Edge should prefer stateless resume (no large buffer) and surface tokens to clients when available.
3) Idempotency-Key required for any full replay attempt; edge will dedupe/bill on Idempotency-Key.
raj: :thumbsup: I can PR the artifacts (header defs + state machine) into the RFC doc.
marco: I'll add the billing section and prefix-caching rules.
zhen: I'll sketch a small upstream shim prototype that emits resume-token checkpoints every ~1s or N tokens.
olivia: Thanks all — will land RFC update with these bullets and link to the prototype. If anyone sees a blocker for canary, shout here. :mag:
marco: nit: we should add a short sentence about trailer authenticity (TLS + conn-level integrity) so proxies don't accept unauthenticated trailers from compromised upstreams.
olivia: Good catch — will add security note. End of thread."
